glama_health.note: RESOLVED. Root cause (R3, confirmed as FACT not guess): src/mcp/server.ts returned a hard 401 on the MCP `initialize` request whenever no Authorization header was present -- exactly how Glama's own connector health-checker probes /mcp, so every probe failed before the handshake could even start. nginx access logs for the Glama prober (IP 40.160.65.14, UA node) show the flip cleanly: daily 401s through 2026-09-21 (zero 200s), 401 x8 on 2026-09-22 before 02:52Z, then from 02:52Z a clean initialize 200 -> initialized 202 -> tools/list 200 handshake (390x/114x that day, 237x/68x on 09-23). Fixed by commit 5df51566 (T-0211, ZZ-03-11), deployed 2026-09-22 02:52Z. Glama's connector Status field read Healthy at 2026-09-23 14:46Z (first confirmed reading). ZZ-03-11 requires a second Healthy reading >=6h later (not before 2026-09-23 20:46Z, tracked separately as T-B) before this counts as durably fixed rather than a one-off lucky crawl. Uptime% shown on the connector page is a rolling window over the prior 35 days of 401s and will climb back up on its own. See docs/OPERATOR-ACTION-registry-listings.md (R3) and disputes/0179-glama-operator-declined-drift-escalation.ruling-1.md. first_seen is kept as history of when the 30-day clock originally started; `resolved` is what check-external-listings.sh's classify() reads to reset that clock to age=0 -- if this ever recurs, commit a fresh first_seen rather than relying on this stale resolved date.

glama_server_listing.note: A different Glama object from glama_health above. This is the SERVER listing (glama.ai/mcp/servers/whiteknightonhorse/APIbase, GitHub-repo-linked, rebuilt via Deploy -> Create Release), not the connector page (glama.ai/mcp/connectors/io.github.whiteknightonhorse/apibase) that glama_health tracks. Republishing this listing is now a paid ($9) operator action; the operator declined to pay for it as of 2026-09-23. The page currently mixes stale numbers (1381/390/618 across its tool/provider counts) and shows a D-grade quality widget; it has no Status field at all, and check-external-listings.sh never checks it -- glama_health only reads the connector's binary Status field. This entry exists for the record only: do not open follow-up tasks for it, do not build a scraper for it, not checked by CI (classify() treats operator-declined as never blocking). See docs/OPERATOR-ACTION-registry-listings.md#T-R4-GLAMA-OPERATOR-DECLINED and disputes/0179-glama-operator-declined-drift-escalation.ruling-1.md.

pulsemcp.note: ZZ-03-10 (D-2/R6). PulseMCP's listing shows materially wrong content ('API development platform with testing, monitoring, and documentation tools' — not a stale number, a wrong description entirely) and the site was, as of 02-RESEARCH.md §2.9/§2.12, refusing new submissions while redesigning listing management. Both the public page and the documented v0.1 API (which additionally needs a key this repo doesn't hold) are Cloudflare-blocked against automated fetches from this repo's CI/server context — check-external-listings.sh reports pulsemcp as unreachable, which is the expected steady state, not a signal to retry. R6 is the operator manually checking PulseMCP's status 7 days after R4 completes, then (if still wrong) sending a fleet-drafted correction request. This entry's 30-day clock is a backstop, not the R6 timeline itself.
